row.title: Submit PSURs for generic, WEU, herbal and homeopathic products where the EURD list requires them
row.statement: Marketing authorisation holders of generic, well-established use, traditional herbal and homeopathic medicinal products must submit PSURs for the active substances that the list of EU reference dates specifies as requiring PSURs for such products.

row.title: Submit PSURs for generic and similar products when a Member State authority requests them
row.statement: Notwithstanding the list of EU reference dates, when a competent authority in a Member State requests PSURs for a generic, well-established use, traditional herbal or homeopathic medicinal product (which it may do at any time under DIR Art 107c(2)), the marketing authorisation holder must submit them.

Row described authorities' practice; the section's company duty is that MAHs shall submit PSURs immediately upon request. Quote extended to include it.

row.title: Submit PSURs immediately upon request from a Member State competent authority
row.statement: Marketing authorisation holders must submit PSURs immediately upon request from a competent authority in a Member State; authorities normally request PSURs via the list of EU reference dates but in special circumstances may request a PSUR directly.
row.quote:
Marketing authorisation holders shall submit PSURs immediately upon request from a competent
authority in a Member State [DIR Art 107c(2)]. To facilitate the EU assessment and avoid duplication
of requests, the competent authorities in the Member States should normally make use of the list of EU
reference dates to request the submission of PSURs, however in especial circumstances competent
authorities in Member States can directly request the submission of a PSUR.

row.title: Treat protocol amendments affecting participant safety or study results as substantial amendments
row.statement: The marketing authorisation holder should treat as a substantial amendment to a PASS protocol any amendment likely to affect the safety, physical or mental well-being of participants or the study results and their interpretation, e.g. changes to objectives, population, sample size, design, data sources, data collection method, main exposure/outcome/confounder definitions or the statistical analysis plan.
